passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: We are a leading retailer and distributor of automotive replacement parts and accessories in the Americas. We began operations in 1979 and at August 30, 2025, operated 6,627 stores in the U.S., 883 stores in Mexico and 147 stores in Brazil. Each store carries an extensive product line for cars, sport utility vehicles, vans and light duty trucks, including new and remanufactured automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products. At August 30, 2025, in 6,098 of our domestic stores as well as the vast majority of our stores in Mexico and Brazil, we had a commercial sales program that provides prompt delivery of parts and other products and commercial credit to local, regional and national repair garages, dealers, service stations, fleet owners and other accounts. We also sell automotive hard parts, maintenance items, accessories and non-automotive products through www.autozone.com, and our commercial customers can make purchases through www.autozonepro.com. Additionally, we sell the ALLDATA brand of automotive diagnostic, repair, collision and shop management software through www.alldata.com. We also provide product information on our Duralast branded products through www.duralastparts.com. We do not derive revenue from automotive repair or installation services. Executive Summary For fiscal 2025, net sales increased to $18.9 billion, a 2.4% increase over the prior year. Domestic commercial sales increased 6.7%, which represents 31.7% of our total Domestic sales . Operating profit decreased 4.7% to $3.6 billion, net income decreased 6.2% to $2.5 billion and diluted earnings per share decreased 3.1% to $144.87 for the year. Fiscal 2025 consisted of 52 weeks whereas fiscal 2024 consisted of 53 weeks. The inclusion of the 53 rd week in fiscal 2024 resulted in an increase to net sales of $365.9 million and an increase in operating profit of $86.7 million. Additionally, fiscal 2025 comparisons were negatively impacted by foreign currency exchange rates which had an unfavorable impact to net sales of $273.1 million and operating profit of $88.2 million. Operating profit comparison was also negatively impacted by an unfavorable net non-cash LIFO impact of $104.0 million. During fiscal 2025, failure and maintenance related categories represented the largest portion of our sales mix, at approximately 85% of total sales. While we have not experienced any fundamental shifts in our category sales mix as compared to previous years, we have seen a slight decrease in mix of sales of the accessories category and a slight increase in the maintenance and failure categories compared to the previous two years. Our business is impacted by various factors within the economy that affect both our consumer and our industry, including but not limited to inflation, interest rates, levels of consumer debt, fuel and energy costs, prevailing wage rates, foreign exchange rate fluctuations, supply chain disruptions, tariffs, trade policies and other geopolitical factors, hiring and other economic conditions. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Our business is subject to a variety of risks and uncertainties. The risks and uncertainties described below could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and stock price. The following information should be read in conjunction with the other information contained in this report and other filings that we make with the SEC. These risks and uncertainties are not the only ones we face. Our business could also be materially affected by additional factors that are presently unknown to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial to our business. Strategic and Operational Risks ​ The current global economic and geopolitical landscape has increased uncertainty about key areas of doing business internationally and may have a negative impact on our business. ​ During fiscal 2025, new global trade tariffs were announced on imports to the United States, including additional tariffs on various countries from which the Company directly or indirectly imports and/or sources merchandise, including Canada, China and Mexico, among others. In response, several countries have imposed or threatened reciprocal tariffs on imports from the U.S. and other measures. Various modifications to the U.S. tariffs have been 13 Table of Contents announced, and further changes are expected to be made in the future, including in response to pending litigation, which may include additional sector-based tariffs or other measures. Additionally, the current administration has directed various federal agencies to further evaluate key aspects of U.S. trade policy and amid ongoing discussion and commentary regarding further potentially significant changes to U.S. trade policies, enforcement priorities, sanctions, treaties and tariffs. As a result of these ongoing developments, significant uncertainty continues with respect to the future economic and political relationship between the U.S. and other countries. The ultimate impact of tariffs and other trade policies on the Company’s business will depend on several factors, including whether additional or incremental U.S. tariffs or other measures are announced, revised, or rescinded, to what extent other countries implement tariffs or other measures in response, the overall magnitude and duration of these measures and our ability to mitigate the impacts of such measures more effectively than our competitors. These developments, or the perception that any of them could occur, may have a material effect on global economic conditions, the stability of global financial markets, or global trade, and may impact the Company’s product cost, pricing, or competitive conditions, disrupt supply chains, impact the broader macroeconomic environment and consumer sentiment or otherwise negatively impact the Company’s business, financial condition and results of operations. ​ If demand for our products slows, then our business may be materially adversely affected. ​ Demand for the products we sell may be affected by a number of factors we cannot control, including: ● the number of older vehicles in service. credit_strengths.text: AutoZone's operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditures, leaving substantial free cash flow that supports debt service and shareholder returns. The business generates stable cash flow from a recession-resistant aftermarket parts model, with failure and maintenance categories comprising the bulk of sales, providing revenue visibility through economic cycles.

Interest coverage remains solid, with operating income covering interest expense multiple times over. This headroom, combined with a long-dated maturity profile and a revolving credit facility that was recently extended, provides financial flexibility. The company's scale and leading market position in the Americas support its intermediate financial risk profile.

key_risks.text: New global trade tariffs on imports from Canada, China, and Mexico, as well as reciprocal measures, introduce cost and supply chain uncertainty. These developments could pressure product costs and pricing, potentially eroding margins if the company cannot fully mitigate the impact, especially given its international sourcing footprint.

The debt structure includes a significant commercial paper balance and sizable maturities within the next twelve months. While the revolving credit facility provides backstop liquidity, reliance on short-term funding exposes the company to refinancing risk if credit markets tighten or rates rise, particularly with a portion of debt maturing in the near term.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow to debt is moderate, indicating that internally generated funds cover a reasonable portion of debt, but not overwhelmingly. The company's ability to service debt relies on sustained operating cash flow, which has been stable. Leverage sits slightly above the sector median, suggesting limited headroom for adverse business conditions.

The maturity profile is manageable, with no single year requiring excessive repayment, and the revolving credit facility provides a liquidity backstop. However, the current ratio is below one, reflecting a working capital deficit typical of retailers, which could constrain financial flexibility if cash flow deteriorates.

overall_credit_view.text: AutoZone's credit profile is supported by its leading market position, stable cash generation, and adequate interest coverage. The intermediate financial risk profile reflects leverage modestly above the sector median and a cash flow-to-debt ratio that is satisfactory but not exceptional. The company's consistent operating performance and long-dated debt maturities mitigate near-term refinancing risk.

However, shareholder distributions absorb a substantial portion of free cash flow, limiting debt reduction capacity. Tariff-related cost pressures and potential demand slowdowns pose risks to margins and cash flow. The company's leverage headroom is limited, and a deterioration in operating performance could pressure the credit profile. Overall, the credit is stable but sensitive to external shocks.

credit_strengths.text: AutoZone的營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下大量自由現金流以支持債務償付及股東回報。該業務憑藉抗衰退的售後零件模式產生穩定現金流，其中故障及維修類別佔銷售大宗，在經濟週期中提供收入可見度。
利息覆蓋率維持穩健，營運收入覆蓋利息開支達數倍以上。此緩衝空間，加上長年期到期結構及近期獲延長的循環信貸融資，提供財務靈活性。該公司在美洲的規模及領先市場地位支持其中等財務風險狀況。

key_risks.text: 對來自加拿大、中國及墨西哥的進口商品徵收的新全球貿易關稅，以及對等措施，帶來成本及供應鏈不確定性。這些發展可能對產品成本及定價構成壓力，若公司無法完全緩解影響，可能侵蝕利潤率，尤其考慮到其國際採購足跡。
債務結構包括顯著的商業票據餘額及未來十二個月內到期的可觀債務。雖然循環信貸融資提供後備流動性，但依賴短期資金使公司面臨再融資風險，若信貸市場收緊或利率上升，尤其是部分債務於短期內到期。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流對債務比率適中，顯示內部產生資金覆蓋合理部分債務，但並非壓倒性。公司償付債務的能力依賴持續營運現金流，而該現金流一直穩定。槓桿略高於行業中位數，顯示應對不利業務狀況的緩衝空間有限。
到期結構可控，並無任何單一年份需要過度還款，而循環信貸融資提供流動性後備。然而，流動比率低於一，反映零售商典型的營運資金赤字，若現金流惡化，可能限制財務靈活性。

overall_credit_view.text: AutoZone的信貸狀況受其領先市場地位、穩定現金產生及充足利息覆蓋支持。中等財務風險狀況反映槓桿略高於行業中位數，以及現金流對債務比率令人滿意但非卓越。公司一貫的營運表現及長年期債務到期結構緩解短期再融資風險。
然而，股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，限制減債能力。關稅相關成本壓力及潛在需求放緩對利潤率及現金流構成風險。公司槓桿緩衝空間有限，營運表現惡化可能對信貸狀況構成壓力。整體而言，信貸穩定但對外部衝擊敏感。
